## Headline #1 — Variance reduction: antithetic sampling plus a control variate

Four arms at equal total path count on an arithmetic-average Asian call, controlled by a European call on the same paths whose expectation is known exactly in closed form. The reduction is quoted **both** as a standard-error reduction and as a variance reduction, because they are the same fact in different units and a bare percentage is ambiguous between them.

### Result

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| Standard error reduction, arm A to arm D | `49.62%` |
| Variance reduction, arm A to arm D | `74.62%` |
| Equivalent path-count speedup<br><sub>paths the crude estimator would need to match arm D's standard error</sub> | `3.94x` |
| Arm A — crude, standard error | `0.017075` |
| Arm B — antithetic, standard error | `0.012792` |

### Inputs

| input | value |
|---|---|
| Product | `arithmetic average Asian call, average over daily closes after inception` |
| Control | `European call on the same paths, same strike and maturity` |
| Total paths per arm | `200,000` |
| Time steps | `252` |
| Chunk size (paths) | `10,000` |
| Pilot paths for beta | `20,000` |
| Market | `div_yield=0.0, rate=0.02, spot=100.0, vol=0.2` |
